name: Temporary, Ordinary, and Privileged Resident Cards

requirements.blocker_text: Foreigners staying beyond 3 months (classified as 'immigrants' rather than 'visitors' under Congo's residence framework) must hold a residence card. The entry-level Temporary Resident card is valid up to 1 year, reported at a fee of 106,000 F CFA -- this dataset could not independently confirm this fee against a government tariff decree.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for the Temporary Resident card once staying beyond 3 months.

requirements.blocker_text: The Ordinary Resident card is valid up to 3 years, reported at a fee of 206,000 F CFA.
requirements.fix_path: Upgrade from the Temporary to the Ordinary Resident card.

requirement_groups.name: Privileged Resident (up to 5 years, 10-year residence gate)

requirements.blocker_text: The Privileged Resident card is valid up to 5 years and requires 10 years of continuous residence in Congo, with the applicant under 35 years old at initial entry -- extended to 40 if married to a Congolese spouse or parent of a legally recognized Congolese child. Reported fee: 106,000 F CFA.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 10 years of continuous residence while meeting the applicable age ceiling at initial entry (35, or 40 with a qualifying Congolese family tie).

evidence_required.document: Housing certificate signed by a municipal authority

outcome.duration_length: 1 year (temporary) -> 3 years (ordinary) -> 5 years (privileged), each renewable within its own tier
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 10 years continuous residence for the Privileged Resident tier

sources.title: Legavox (Yav & Associates law firm) -- Congo's three-tier resident card system: Temporary (1yr), Ordinary (3yr), Privileged (5yr, 10yr-residence + age gate), fees, required documents

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Congo-Brazzaville). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier-3 sourced (a law-firm legal-advice blog; detailed and internally consistent, but not a primary government text). This dataset attempted direct fetches of Congo's own Ministry of Interior (interieur.gouv.cg) and Ministry of Public Security (securite-publique.gouv.cg), both of which have a dedicated 'Titre de Séjour' page per search results, but every fetch attempt failed (SSL certificate error on one, DNS resolution failure on the other) -- a genuine, disclosed fetch failure, not a claim the pages are wrong or don't exist. GENUINE STRUCTURAL FINDING, distinct from every other country built in this dataset to date: a real 3-tier numeric residence ladder (1yr/3yr/5yr) PLUS an unusual AGE-based eligibility ceiling stacked on top of the residence-duration gate for the top tier (under 35 at entry, extended to 40 for a Congolese family tie) -- this age-ceiling mechanic has not appeared in any other country built in this session, including Cameroon's comparable 2-tier ladder (2yr/10yr) which has no age condition.
